items.text: Can explain what a user is in Linux and list the 6 components of a user account
Can name and describe the three types of Linux users (root, normal, system)
Know the UID ranges: 0 = root, 1–999 = system, 1000+ = normal
Know which three files in /etc store user information and what each contains
Understand the difference between primary group and secondary groups
Can explain how sudo works and why it is safer than logging in as root
Can create a user with useradd and immediately set a password with passwd
Can safely add a user to a secondary group using usermod -aG
Understand the dangerous difference between usermod -G and usermod -aG
Can create groups with groupadd and verify with cat /etc/group
Can delete a user and their home directory with userdel -r
Can SSH into an EC2 instance using a .pem key file
Can verify user and group changes using the id command
Can recall the wheel group (RHEL/CentOS/Amazon Linux) vs sudo group (Ubuntu/Debian) difference
Know that root UID is always 0 and can explain why
Know the SSH public key location: ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
